questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Manager's Commission Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: Remuneration allowed to a manager calculated as a percentage of net profits, either before or after charging such commission.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Manager's Commission Adjustment'.
questions.a: Commission before charging uses rate/100; commission after charging uses rate/(100 + rate).

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Manager's Commission Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: commission = profit * rate / 100 OR commission = profit * rate / (100 + rate)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Interest on Capital Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: Interest allowed to the proprietor on capital invested in business, treated as a business expense in P&L and credited to capital account in Balance Sheet.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Interest on Capital Adjustment'.
questions.a: Interest on capital is charged to profit and loss account as an expense and added to capital in the balance sheet.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Interest on Capital Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: interest_on_capital = capital * rate / 100

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Interest on Capital Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: An adjustment made to record interest allowed on the owner's capital investment, which is treated as an expense for the business and an addition to capital.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Interest on Capital Adjustment'.
questions.a: Increases business expenses (debit P&L) and increases owner's capital in the balance sheet.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Interest on Capital Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: interest_on_capital = capital * rate / 100

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Interest on Drawings' refers to.
questions.a: Interest charged by the business on withdrawals made by the owner for personal use, which is an income for the business and a deduction from capital.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Interest on Drawings'.
questions.a: Credited to P&L account and deducted from drawings/capital in the balance sheet.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Interest on Drawings', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: interest_on_drawings = drawings * rate / 100

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Access DLookup Function' refers to.
questions.a: An Access database function used to search and retrieve a specific value from a field in a table or query based on a given search condition.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Access DLookup Function'.
questions.a: Retrieves non-local data for display in forms or reports.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Access DLookup Function', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: value = DLookup(field_name, table_name, criteria)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Access DSum Function' refers to.
questions.a: A domain aggregate function in Access that calculates and returns the sum of values in a specified field or expression within a table or query, optionally filtered by a criteria.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Access DSum Function'.
questions.a: Computes totals for a subset of records matching a condition.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Access DSum Function', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: total_sum = DSum(expression, table_name, criteria)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Access IIF Function' refers to.
questions.a: A conditional function in Access that evaluates a logical expression and returns one value if the expression is true, and another value if it is false.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Access IIF Function'.
questions.a: Implements binary decision logic in queries, forms, or reports.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Access IIF Function', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: result = IIF(condition, value_if_true, value_if_false)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Access Val Function' refers to.
questions.a: A function that extracts and returns the numeric characters from a string as a numeric value, stopping at the first non-numeric character.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Access Val Function'.
questions.a: Converts string representations of numbers into actual numeric types.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Access Val Function', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: numeric_value = Val(string_expression)
